title: U.S. House · California's 45th District
area: Southern Los Angeles and northern Orange counties, including Little Saigon-area cities such as Garden Grove and Westminster. Redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025), the district shifted several more Democratic areas of Los Angeles County into the seat.

context.text: Incumbent Derek Tran (D) and Republican Chuong Vo advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary; Tran received 52.5% of the vote to a combined 47.5% for Vo and four other Republicans. Analyst Nathaniel Rakich of Inside Elections said redistricting moved the seat from D+1 to D+5 while noting it should remain competitive. As of August 2026, election forecasters rated the general election Likely, Lean or Tilt Democratic.

candidates.name: Derek Tran
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 52.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Derek Tran is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in the 45th District, first elected in 2024. He is a U.S. Army veteran, consumer-rights attorney and small-business (pharmacy) owner.

background.text: Born in Los Angeles County, California; earned a bachelor's degree from Bentley University and a law degree from Glendale University.
Served eight years in the U.S. Army.
Worked as a consumer-rights attorney and co-owns a local pharmacy with his wife.

priorities.text: Protecting abortion rights and access to Planned Parenthood and other women's health services.
Defending Medicare and Medicaid, and lowering the cost of health care and prescription drugs.
Investing in public schools, early childhood education and vocational/job training.

positions.summary: Describes himself as 100% pro-choice and says he has worked to protect funding for Planned Parenthood and access to birth control and cancer screenings.
Says he has worked to rein in the cost of health care and prescription drugs and opposed Republican efforts to cut Medicaid, and will continue defending Medicare.

record.text: Serves on House committees for the 2025-2026 term (assignments listed on his Ballotpedia profile).

candidates.name: Chuong Vo
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary as the leading Republican candidate.

summary.text: Chuong Vo is the Republican candidate in the 45th District. He is a retired Torrance Police Department officer and former Cerritos City Council member.

background.text: Worked as a law-enforcement officer with the Torrance Police Department from 1999 to 2025.
Served on the executive board of the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority between 2021 and 2025.
Served on the Cerritos City Council from 2020 to 2025.

priorities.text: Public safety, including support for law enforcement and targeting organized retail theft and fentanyl trafficking.
Lowering the cost of living by cutting wasteful federal spending while protecting Social Security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Says he will always back law enforcement and push to fully fund training and equipment so officers and federal agents can do their jobs safely.

Says he supports secure borders and faster, better-resourced asylum and enforcement processing, while also calling for modernizing legal immigration so families and employers can follow an orderly process.
